name: Stat Count Up
summary: A big number counts or ticks up at the centre of a styled backdrop and lands on the headline figure, with a short label, timed to the narration saying it. It turns a claim into proof the viewer can feel.
when_to_use: Backing a claim with a single headline metric such as scale, speed or coverage
Showing an outcome as a before and after number
Landing a proof beat right after a feature has been shown

slots.name: stat_value
slots.what: the final figure, with an optional suffix such as plus, percent or times

slots.name: start_value
slots.what: where the count begins; a lower number, or zero

slots.name: label
slots.what: a short caption saying what the number measures

slots.name: backdrop
slots.what: a gradient or brand field, with optional ambient shapes, logos or chips drifting behind

slots.name: second_stat
slots.what: an optional second figure that joins the first side by side

slots.name: context_ui
slots.what: a dashboard or card the number lives in, when the stat sits inside product interface

steps: Reveal the backdrop with its slow ambient drift
Fade or blur the number in at the centre
Count it up quickly, easing out, to land on the final figure as the narration says it
Bring in the label and hold while the backdrop keeps drifting
Optionally reframe to make room for a second stat
Exit with a zoom through, a wipe, a flash or a slide

build.gsap: One timeline per scene. Tween a plain object's value and write it into the number element on update, rounded and formatted with tabular figures, using a power or expo out ease so the count slows as it lands; blur and fade the number in just before. Loop slow linear or sine drifts on the backdrop layers at different speeds. For a second stat, tween the first card's width and slide the second card in from the edge with a power out ease.
build.remotion: A Sequence for the stat where interpolate maps frame to value with an ease-out and the number is formatted per frame; a spring drives the number's entrance scale; background layers use per-layer interpolate on translate for parallax; a later Sequence handles the reframe or the exit.

sound: Music carries the scene; a chime is the most common clear cue and tends to land as the number settles, and a reverse swoosh often builds into the reveal. Impacts are occasional, later in the scene.
caveats: Few shots, and first-motion timing comes from only a handful of them.
Members are mixed: some count up, some count down or flip cards, and some hold a static stat card with no count.
Clear sound cues such as the chime come from only a couple of videos.
